claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Robert E. Schukraft is confirmed as the career Signal Corps officer documented in official congressional and Army Security Agency records.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name, compatible wartime rank, Signal Corps chronology and protected officer identifier agree across official records.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact uncommon name, compatible rank, direct wartime testimony and protected officer-identifier agreement with the later official history.
claims.temporal_assessment: The congressional affidavit documents his Army assignment before Pearl Harbor and his June 1945 Signal Intelligence assignment; it does not date entry into OSS.
claims.match_notes: The protected officer identifier is retained privately and masked in public data. No civilian employer is inferred for this career officer.

claims.claim_text: On December 7, 1941 and for an unspecified period beforehand, Robert E. Schukraft was the Army Signal Intelligence Service officer in charge of radio intercepts in Washington.

claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact person in sworn official testimony, corroborated by the indexed rank and protected officer identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly in place on December 7, 1941 and for some time beforehand; definitely pre-OSS-era evidence, but not proved to be immediately before his OSS relationship.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The last civilian employer and exact OSS transfer sequence remain unknown.
